# Awesome Omni Architectures [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

<!-- Generated by scripts/catalog.py from data/models.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

A source-backed catalog of omni models, spoken language models (SpeechLMs), audio-language understanding, LLM-based ASR and language-model-based speech generation.

**Research snapshot: 2026-09-12. 356 main catalog entries and 12 related entries.** Entries represent named models, meaningful generations or explicitly identified systems; they are not a count of unique base architectures or downloadable checkpoints.

This is a broad, maintained literature and release inventory. Public evidence cannot establish an exhaustive list of every private model, derivative fine-tune, checkpoint or future release. Historical and preview models remain useful research references; inclusion does not imply current API availability or released weights.

[Model index](#models) · [Taxonomy](#taxonomy) · [Dated sources](docs/timeline.md) · [Research methodology](docs/methodology.md) · [JSON catalog](data/models.json) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)

Each category includes primary-source links, architecture summaries, input/output modalities, interaction modes, source dates and variant notes. The [JSON](data/models.json) also records source titles and review levels.

## Taxonomy

Omni is used inconsistently in the literature. Here the main omni section covers language models that combine audio/speech with vision, including understanding-only models and labeled systems. SpeechLM coverage also includes speech-only foundations, speech/text assistants and LM-based synthesizers.

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| T / I / V | Text / image / video. |
| A / S / M | General audio / speech / music. Speech and music are audio subtypes, not additional independent modalities. |
| X | Other representations such as grounding coordinates, motion, sensors or actions; described in the entry. |
| text-output | Listed task produces text or structured text; no audio generation is asserted. |
| generation | Conditional generation or continuation; no real-time interaction guarantee. |
| streaming | A source documents incremental processing or generation; this does not establish simultaneous listening and speaking. |
| full-duplex | A source explicitly describes concurrent listening and spoken output. This is a reported capability, not an independently reproduced measurement. |
| system | The entry coordinates multiple components, models or external generators. |
| not-specified | The reviewed evidence does not establish a more specific interaction mode. |

Modality columns describe capabilities documented for the named entry; family rows may span variants. Consult variant notes and the exact checkpoint/API documentation before choosing an implementation. Reference speech for TTS is conditioning, not evidence of spoken question answering. See the [scope rules and architecture guide](docs/methodology.md).

## Research and maintenance

The [methodology](docs/methodology.md) documents the discovery sources, inclusion rules, naming corrections and review limits. The [timeline](docs/timeline.md) uses paper/announcement dates and keeps undated entries separate. These dates are not model release dates.

Edit `data/models.json`, then regenerate the Markdown views and check consistency:

```bash
python3 scripts/catalog.py
python3 scripts/catalog.py --check
```

The validator checks identifiers, modality labels, source metadata, dates, generated-file freshness and local Markdown links. It runs offline and does not test model inference or live endpoint availability. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for adding a model and the [optional architecture article template](templates/model-template.md) for deeper write-ups.
